name: China economy
summary: Factory PMI back in contraction; regulators reportedly pause IPOs amid stock sell-off
state: Chinese regulators told banks to pause IPOs and large share sales to steady a falling stock market, the FT reported on 3 Nov, after a 2 Nov pledge to support the capital market. The official manufacturing PMI fell to 49.3 in October (31 Oct). Q3 GDP grew 4.5%, near target, with no sign of financial contagion or capital controls as of 3 Nov.
for_you: Chinese demand affects commodity prices and exporters' earnings; no direct effect on households elsewhere yet.
rubric_hit: Growth near target; no defaults wave or contagion

sources.title: Newsquawk — China regulators tell banks to pause IPOs (FT)

why: China is the world's factory and the biggest marginal buyer of commodities; a hard landing would ripple through every supply chain.
drivers: Property sector, local-government debt, exports and tariffs, deflation, stimulus.

rubric.alert: Hard landing (growth < 3%), financial contagion, or capital controls tightened sharply.
rubric.watch: Deflation, renewed property-developer defaults, or growth clearly below target.
rubric.normal: Growth near official target, stable property sales, no financial contagion.
